shared_context.content: For n >= 0, define (q;q)_0 := 1 and (q;q)_n := product_{t=1}^n (1 - q^t).
shared_context.label: q-factorial

shared_context.content: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, define R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a).
shared_context.label: interval-ratio

shared_context.content: [q^j]F(q) denotes the coefficient of q^j in a polynomial or formal power series F(q).
shared_context.label: coefficient-notation

shared_context.content: A partition with parts in {a+1,...,b} means a finite multiset lambda of elements of {a+1,...,b}; |lambda| denotes the sum of its parts.

strategy_summary: Reduce the theorem to a signed combinatorial counting problem. First pass from the q-factorial quotient to its formal power-series expansion. Then use cyclotomic factorization to extract an arithmetic divisibility-dominance condition from the assumption that the quotient is a polynomial. Express each target coefficient as a signed count of subset-partition pairs. The genuine hard step is then isolated as a sign-reversing involution on that signed set for degrees j up to floor(r(b-a)/2). A generic involution lemma converts that involution into coefficient nonnegativity.
